content:
The image shows a very young soybean seedling at emergence stage in wet soil. Key observations:

- **Plant part**: Seedling/germination stage (cotyledon/seed visible at soil surface)
- **Key features**:
  - Wet, saturated soil conditions
  - One seedling emerging with small leaves (partially healthy)
  - The seed/cotyledon to the right is visibly brown, rotted, and collapsed — pre/post-emergence damping off
  - The hypocotyl shows signs of decay
  - Classic wet soil + rotted seed scenario

**Reasoning**: The rotted seed/cotyledon at soil level in saturated soil is the hallmark of pre/post-emergence damping off. Pythium thrives in wet, cool soils and causes seed rot and seedling collapse at this exact stage. Rhizoctonia typically shows a distinct sunken reddish-brown lesion on the hypocotyl (wire-stem), which is not the dominant feature here. Phytophthora damping off is possible but Pythium is most associated with the saturated soil + seed rot presentation seen here.
